title: Migration, as a Skill
whyThisDirection: Refraction had the highest combined score from the three judges (7.5 / 7.5 / 8). It already has keynote-scale type, no terminal chrome, one strict left-to-right ember-to-ice rule and the lowest risk of looking like a vendor's UI, so it is the base. It lacked a pain beat the viewer can feel and a team payoff. To fill those gaps I took four pieces from the other concepts: Maya's story spine (the same 12-tile board before and after through a match cut, 'Needs you' tiles, beams to teammates), Open the Skill's 'Playbook · Mappings · Checks' triptych, which uses the user's own words, Write It Once's stepped 'by hand' motion, and its NULLS LAST trap, used as the single tool-agnostic code moment. Following the 'just high level' direction, I removed every product and API name, every file tree, diff and terminal log, the clock and all speed-up numbers.

alternatives.title: 12 Spark Jobs. One Request.
alternatives.oneLine: One-take 3D camera through a glass terminal. One typed request, then the skill loads, swaps sessions, catches a time-zone drift and ends in a freeze-wave tile flip.
alternatives.verdict: Not used as the base. It is terminal-heavy, names Snowpark Connect, runs 10 beats, has no pain beat and its one-take camera is expensive. Kept: its hook rhythm and the freeze-wave tile flip, simplified to one gradient sheen.

alternatives.title: Write It Once: Spark to Snowflake, Split Screen
alternatives.oneLine: A glowing seam splits one job into 'without the skill' (re-pasted rules, one missed, wrong row wins) and 'with the skill' (one request, same steps, self-checks).
alternatives.verdict: Not used as the base. The split halves type size, the pasted-rules side reads as a straw man, and it has three code moments. Kept: the stepped 'by hand' motion and the NULLS LAST trap as the only code.

alternatives.title: Open the Skill: Spark → Snowflake
alternatives.oneLine: One glass slab opens as a triptych (playbook / map / check) and then pays off in Load, Convert and Verify beats.
alternatives.verdict: Kept: the triptych, now titled 'Playbook · Mappings · Checks', as the single 'what is a skill' frame. Dropped: no pain beat, API-named mapping rows, the diff, and a claim of 12/12 converted despite an RDD job.

alternatives.title: Refraction: Migration, as a Skill
alternatives.oneLine: Keynote motion graphics: ember Spark cards pass through a glass skill and leave as ice Snowflake jobs, with two flagged for a human.
alternatives.verdict: CHOSEN BASE. Kept its type grammar, prompt pill (no terminal), warm-to-cool rule and 'Migration, as a skill.' end line. Changes: added a pain beat and a team beat, and removed the 9-line diff, API pills and context meter.

alternatives.title: Maya's Ticket: 40 Spark Jobs, One Skill
alternatives.oneLine: One engineer's ticket: repeated questions swirl into a Skill, one plain request, a match-cut wave, and the whole team reuses it.
alternatives.verdict: Kept as the story spine: pain board, notes swirling into a folder, the match-cut wave, 'Needs you' tiles and teammate beams. Dropped the named character, ticket ID, clock, 40 tiles, diff and dense UI.

style.typography:
All fonts load offline: npm @fontsource woff2 files are copied into public/ and loaded with @remotion/fonts loadFont({family, url: staticFile(...)}), with rendering held by delayRender until they resolve. Do not use @remotion/google-fonts, which fails in this container.
- DISPLAY: Inter Tight 800 (@fontsource/inter-tight 5.3.0). Headlines are 120px by default (160px for 'Just ask.', 112px minimum), letter-spacing -0.04em, line-height 0.95, always one line, fitText max width 1500px. The key word in each headline takes the signature gradient plus a 24px glow at 35%.
- ACCENT: Instrument Serif Italic 400 (@fontsource/instrument-serif 5.3.0) for exactly two words, 'once' (S2) and 'skill' (S3, S8), at 1.08x the headline size so it matches optically, with gradient fill.
- TEXT: Inter Tight 500 at 44px for sub-captions (Slate); 700 at 48px for triptych titles; 500 at 28px for glosses; 600 at 18-20px UPPERCASE with +0.14em tracking for pills and chips ('SPARK', 'SNOWFLAKE', 'NEEDS YOU', 'DEMO PROJECT'); 500 at 20px for the footnote.
- MONO: JetBrains Mono 500/700 (@fontsource/jetbrains-mono, render-verified in the probe), ligatures off. Prompt 40px, S6 code 48px, tile filenames 22px, stat chips 30px with tabular-nums, status line 26px, folder tab and end mono line 24-28px.
- FALLBACK: Inter (@fontsource/inter, render-verified in the probe) if Inter Tight has any issue. Inter Tight and Instrument Serif are confirmed on npm at 5.3.0 but were not render-tested in the probe.
style.motionLanguage:
EASING: EXPO_OUT = Easing.bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) for every reveal and camera move (18-24f). EXIT = Easing.bezier(0.7,0,0.84,0) over 10f. Only typing and the light-axis draw are linear.
SPRINGS:
- GLIDE {damping:200}: panels, pills, float-forward. No bounce.
- SNAP {mass:0.8, damping:14, stiffness:120}: tiles, cards, chips, badges. Small premium overshoot.
- HINGE {stiffness:260, damping:14}: triptych hinges and folder lid. About 3° overshoot.
TEXT: per-word masked reveal (translateY 40→0, blur 16→0px, opacity 0→1, 4f stagger, 20f EXPO_OUT). Exit: opacity→0, y -16px, blur 0→8px over 10f. Only one headline on screen at a time, each held at least 1.5s.
TYPING: 2f per character for the prompt and the inserted ' NULLS LAST'; 1f per character for status lines, the folder tab and the code line. Caret blinks every 15f.
CAMERA: no one-take camera. Each shot drifts slowly (scale 1.00→1.03, ±0.3° rotation). Push-ins and pull-backs use EXPO_OUT over 18f.
PAIN VS SKILL: in S1 the ember layer runs on stepped time, pf = Math.floor(frame/3)*3, with seeded ±2px jitter, so it feels manual. From S2 on, everything runs at smooth 30fps. The motion quality alone says 'by hand' versus 'with the skill'.
MOTION BLUR: velocity-driven SVG feGaussianBlur with stdDeviation 'v 0' along the direction of travel, on flying notes, the card flight, push-ins and pull-backs. No CameraMotionBlur.
DEPTH:
- Three parallax planes: orbs/grid/grain at 0.3x, hero objects at 1x, ember and ice bokeh specks at 1.3x.
- Unfocused objects get 6-10px depth-of-field blur, applied to leaf elements only, never to a preserve-3d ancestor.
- Glow comes from blurred duplicates with mix-blend-mode: screen.
- 3D tilt only while tiles flip (≤6° at mid-flip) and on hinges. Anything that must be read is flat.
COLOUR ARC: two huge blurred orbs, ember at bottom-left and ice at top-right, crossfade with interpolateColors on the global frame, from 70/30 ember at f0 to 20/80 ice at f1110. The whole frame cools as the migration happens.
GRAIN: 4-6 feTurbulence PNGs pre-rendered with `remotion still`, cycled every 2f at 3.5% overlay (required, because dark gradients band).
TRANSITIONS:
- Mostly continuous match cuts: tiles → notes → folder → triptych → shelf card; the S1 board and the S5 board share identical layout constants; tile → code panel push-in; board → mini board pull-back.
- A custom 12f diagonal light-wipe overlay (a band of ember → white-hot → ice with bloom) covers the cuts at S4→S5 and S7→S8. It is drawn as an overlay across the boundary with a hard cut underneath at its midpoint, so there are no TransitionSeries overlap frames.
- No shader transitions and no stock slide or wipe.
SFX (optional, local files): stepped paper ticks in S1, a whoosh on each flight, a soft snap on the lid, glassy ticks on the tile flips (quantised to 1 per 3 tiles), a mint chime on the stat chips.
style.layout:
Canvas 1920×1080, 30fps, 1110 frames (37.0s), bt709. Title-safe margin 96px on all sides (content box x96-1824, y96-984). 12-column grid: 122px columns, 24px gutters, inside the 96px margins.
ZONES:
- Headline band: centred at x960, cap-centre y≈190 (y110-270).
- Hero zone: y300-880, centred on a persistent 1px light axis at y=600.
- Sub/stat band: y890-950, centred.
- DEMO PROJECT chip: bottom-left at x96, baseline y980 (S1-S7).
- Footnote (S8 only): centred at baseline y980.
FIXED OBJECTS (share these constants between scenes so match cuts line up):
- BOARD: 4×3 tiles, each 300×170 with radius 18, 28px gaps. Total 1284×566, centred at (960,600).
- TRIPTYCH: 3 panels, each 440×320, 16px gaps (1352×320), centred at (960,600).
- PROMPT PILL: x120-900, y552-648, radius 48.
- SKILL SHELF: 4 cards, each 760×76 with 16px gaps, x1000-1760, y420-772.
- SKILL DOCK (S5-S6): vertical glass strip, 120×320, at x96-216, y440-760.
- CODE PANEL (S6): 1280×400 centred at (960,600). Code starts at x380; the pill stack sits at x1380-1540.
- S7 MINI BOARDS: board at 0.34 scale, centred at (500,440) You, (1420,440) Leo, (500,820) Priya, (1420,820) Sam. Folder hub at (960,630).
- S8 END STACK: folder at (960,340); headline cap-centre y560; sub y660; mono line y730.
LAYERING: every layer is its own AbsoluteFill (bg orbs/grid → grain → light axis → hero objects → cursor/chips → headline → persistent chips), because the probe showed an absolute background can paint over a static SVG.
If a voice-over is added, no burned-in subtitles are needed: each VO line restates the on-screen headline.

scenes.purpose: HOOK + PAIN. Within 1s: a batch of Spark jobs. By 3-5s: migrating them by hand means the same fixes again and again, and one gets missed.
scenes.visual: Dark stage with ember-heavy orbs. A 4×3 wall of 12 glass job tiles, each with an ember 'SPARK' pill, a filename and three faint code-silhouette bars. A white cursor tagged 'you' works through tiles one at a time in stuttery, stepped motion, stamping the same three chips on each. The third tile is left with an empty dashed slot and a coral 'missed one' tag.
scenes.onScreenText:
Headline A (0.3-2.8s): 12 Spark jobs.
Headline B (2.8-5.0s): Same fixes. Every job.
Tile chips: Rewrite · Fix · Test
Stamp: again
Tile tag (tile 2): missed one
Tile filenames (texture, row-major): daily_sales.py · orders_clean.py · latest_customers.sql · events_stream.py · fx_rates.py · refunds.py · inventory.py · churn_model.py · sessions_daily.py · top_products.py · returns_weekly.py · revenue_by_region.py
Corner chip: DEMO PROJECT
scenes.vo: Twelve Spark jobs. By hand, it's the same fixes, job after job.
scenes.animationNotes:
Global f0-150 (local lf = frame within scene).
- lf0-10: the light axis (1px, signature gradient, 40px bloom) draws left to right via evolvePath with EXPO_OUT.
- lf4-34: the 12 tiles cascade in with delay (row+col)×2f. SNAP spring from translateZ -200, blur 12px, opacity 0.
- lf8: word-reveal of '12 Spark jobs.' ('Spark' in the ember gradient). Headlines stay smooth, not stepped.
- From lf30 the ember layer runs on stepped time pf = Math.floor(f/3)*3 with seeded ±2px jitter.
- lf30: the cursor hops to tile 0. Chips 'Rewrite', 'Fix', 'Test' stamp on at lf36/42/48 (stepped scale 1.3→1), and a slow ember progress bar crawls under the tile.
- lf60: the cursor hops to tile 1. The same three chips stamp again while ghosts of tile 0's chips linger at 30%, and a tilted 'again' stamp lands at lf78.

- lf120: a coral dot and the 'missed one' tag pop on with a 4f stepped glitch shake.
- lf120-150: hold. The DEMO PROJECT chip has sat at 60% opacity since lf20.

scenes.purpose: THE IDEA. Those repeated fixes become know-how written once, collected into one folder.
scenes.visual: The board dims into the background. All the repeated chip notes peel off the tiles and swirl along curved paths into one glass folder rising at centre. The notes turn from ember to violet as they cross its rim. The lid snaps shut with a white-hot flash and a gradient shockwave ring, and the folder tab reads spark-to-snowflake/. Motion is smooth from here on.
scenes.onScreenText:
Headline: Write the know-how once.
Folder tab: spark-to-snowflake/
scenes.vo: So write that know-how down, once.
scenes.animationNotes:
Global f150-270.
- lf0-15: the board dims (opacity 1→0.35, scale 1→0.96, 8px blur applied to each tile leaf). The cursor fades out.
- lf6-60: the 8 chip notes (3+3+2) peel off (rotateX -25°, translateZ +80) and fly along seeded cubic Bézier paths (getPointAtLength), with velocity-driven directional blur. The destination is a glass folder springing up (GLIDE) to (960,620) from y+220. Each note recolours from ember to violet as it reaches the rim (interpolateColors on distance) and sets off a small violet flash. The dashed empty slot stays behind on tile 2.
- lf10: word-reveal of 'Write the know-how once.' ('once' in Instrument Serif Italic with the signature gradient).
- lf72-84: the lid snaps shut (rotateX, HINGE spring, about 3° overshoot).
- lf84: a 2f white-hot flash and a shockwave ring (@remotion/shapes circle, gradient stroke, r 80→560, opacity 1→0 over 20f).
- lf84-114: the tab label 'spark-to-snowflake/' types at 1f/char (JetBrains Mono 28px).
- lf114-120: the folder breathes (noise2D ±4px).

scenes.purpose: WHAT A SKILL IS, in one frame: a folder with a playbook, mappings and checks that an AI agent can use. This is also the screenshot moment.
scenes.visual: The folder turns to face the camera and becomes a glass slab. Two white-hot seams split it, and it swings open like a triptych with light pouring through the hinges. It settles as three panels: Playbook, Mappings and Checks, each with a thin-stroke icon, a short gloss and a small file hint. Checks is smoked black glass with a sealed seam (its code is never shown), and a small '✓ match' ticket slides out beneath it.
scenes.onScreenText:
Headline: That's an agent skill.
Panel 1: Playbook · Steps to follow · SKILL.md
Panel 2: Mappings · Spark → Snowflake · references/
Panel 3: Checks · Old vs new must match · scripts/
Ticket under panel 3: ✓ match
scenes.vo: That's an agent skill: a playbook, mappings, and checks, in one folder.
scenes.animationNotes:
Global f270-420.
- lf0-10: the S2 headline exits.
- lf0-20: the folder turns face-on and scales 1→1.35 (GLIDE), becoming a 1352×320 slab.
- lf16: two thin white-hot seams appear at 1/3 and 2/3 of the slab.
- lf24-60: the triptych opens. The left and right panels start folded over the centre panel (rotateY ±180°, transform-origin on the inner hinge edges, preserve-3d, backface-visibility hidden) and swing to 0° with the HINGE spring. Bloom spills through the seams (screen-blend duplicates). The camera pulls back 6%. No filter goes on the preserve-3d parent.
- lf30: word-reveal of 'That's an agent skill.' ('skill' in Instrument Serif Italic with the gradient).
- lf48 / lf66 / lf84: panel contents reveal left to right (18f each, EXPO_OUT): icon (list / two-way arrow / check-in-box, drawn on with evolvePath), title, gloss, mono file hint in Dim. The panel being revealed is at full brightness and the others at 70%. From lf102 all are at 100%.
- lf100-112: the '✓ match' ticket slides out of the Checks panel's bottom edge (SNAP), showing that the script runs and only a result comes back.
- lf112-150: hold with slow drift.

scenes.purpose: HOW YOU USE IT: one plain request. The agent sees every installed skill's one-line summary and opens only the one that matches.
scenes.visual: The triptych snaps shut, shrinks to a one-line card and flies onto a shelf of four one-line skill cards on the right. On the left, a flat glass prompt pill (no terminal chrome) types the request. On Enter, the words 'Migrate' and 'Snowflake' glow, a violet beam links them to the spark-to-snowflake card, and that card lifts with a 'matched' tag while the others dim. The card grows a row of three micro icons, and only Playbook lights up. A status line types under the pill.

scenes.purpose: THE RESULT (signature shot). The same 12-job board from S1 is converted and checked in one wave. Two hard jobs are handed to the human, who reviews everything.
scenes.visual: A light-wipe cuts straight back to the exact S1 board, all ember. The matched card collapses into a vertical skill dock on the left. A diagonal violet-white light band sweeps from the dock across the board, and the tiles flip one after another from ember 'SPARK' to ice 'SNOWFLAKE'. Mint checks draw on 10 tiles; 2 land amber with 'Needs you'. The tile missed in S1 lands ice with a small violet sparkle. Stat chips pop in under the board. Then the 'you' cursor comes back, now moving smoothly, skims across every tile and settles on the two amber tiles, which float forward into a soft spotlight.
scenes.onScreenText:

Headline B (22.2-25.0s): It converts. You review.
Tile pills: SPARK → SNOWFLAKE
Amber tags (events_stream.py, churn_model.py): Needs you
Stat chips: 10 converted · 10/10 match · test data · 2 need you
Corner chip: DEMO PROJECT
scenes.vo: Ten jobs converted and checked. The two hard ones come to you.

scenes.purpose: WHY IT'S TRUSTWORTHY. The skill's mappings catch a real trap that is easy to miss by hand, and it pays off S1's 'missed one'. This is the only code moment.
scenes.visual: The camera pushes into the latest_customers.sql tile, which becomes a flat code panel showing one line of SQL. Next to it, a stack of three pills shows which row wins. Copied as-is to Snowflake, the NULL row jumps to the top ('wrong row'). A violet 'from Mappings' chip arrives, ' NULLS LAST' types in mint, and the NULL row drops back down ('right row').
scenes.onScreenText:
Headline: It knows the traps.
Sub-caption: Spark and Snowflake sort NULLs differently.
Label chip: Spark SQL → as-is on Snowflake
Code: ORDER BY updated_at DESC → ORDER BY updated_at DESC NULLS LAST
Pill stack: Sep 01 · Aug 15 · NULL
Stack label: on Spark → as-is on Snowflake
Tags: wrong row → right row
Chip: from Mappings
scenes.vo: It even knows the traps, like how NULLs sort.

scenes.purpose: TEAM REUSE. The skill is shared once and every teammate's migration follows the same playbook, with hard cases still flagged.
scenes.visual: The camera pulls back fast. The full board shrinks into the 'You' mini board, and the skill folder rises at centre as a glowing hub. Gradient beams draw from the folder to three teammate mini boards, each tagged with a coloured cursor. Each mini board runs the same diagonal ember-to-ice wave, and each lands with exactly one amber tile.

Chip under folder: shared in your repo
Cursor tags: You · Leo · Priya · Sam
scenes.vo: Share it. Your whole team uses it.

scenes.purpose: END CARD. The takeaway in one line, plus an honest footnote.
scenes.visual: A light-wipe clears to a calm end stage, cool and ice-dominant. The skill folder floats at centre with an edge light orbiting its rim. The title builds word by word and an ember-to-ice gradient sweeps through it, followed by the subline, a small mono line and the footnote.
scenes.onScreenText:
Headline: Migration, as a skill.
Sub: Write once. Reuse on every job.
Mono line: spark-to-snowflake/ · playbook · mappings · checks
Footnote: Illustrative demo. Some Spark code needs a redesign, not a conversion. Validate on your own workload.
scenes.animationNotes:

BACKING FILE (never shown as YAML on screen; use it if the companion folder is published in the repo):
---
name: spark-to-snowflake
description: Migrate Spark jobs to Snowflake. Use when asked to migrate or convert Spark code.
---
1. Scan every job in the given folder.
2. Convert each job using references/mappings.md (e.g. add NULLS LAST where Spark SQL relied on DESC default ordering).
3. Flag jobs that need a redesign (e.g. streaming, ML) instead of converting them.
4. Run scripts/check.py on test data. Old and new outputs must match. Report every diff for human review.

Structure mapping (accurate to the Agent Skills format): Playbook = SKILL.md (name + description frontmatter and instructions), Mappings = a reference file that is read only when needed, Checks = a bundled script the agent runs; only the script's result comes back.

(There is no terminal window. Line 1 is the S4 glass prompt pill. Line 2 is the status line typed under the pill in S4. Lines 3-5 appear in S5 as the three stat chips under the board. Every count comes from one demoData constants file: jobs 12, converted 10, needYou 2 [events_stream.py, churn_model.py], checksPassed 10/10, trapTile latest_customers.sql.)
accuracyNotes: Agent Skill anatomy is shown accurately with no jargon. Playbook = SKILL.md (frontmatter with name and description, plus instructions); Mappings = a reference file under references/; Checks = a bundled script under scripts/. The name 'spark-to-snowflake' is valid (lowercase letters and hyphens, at most 64 characters), and the description says both what the skill does and when to use it.

Loading on demand: the shelf shows every installed skill's name and one-line description, which the agent always has. On a matching request only that skill opens and only Playbook lights (SKILL.md read). Mappings lights when conversion uses it and Checks lights when the script runs. The Checks panel is sealed and only a result ('✓ match') comes out, because script code never enters the agent's context. The S4 caption says 'opens', not 'loads', so it does not imply the other skills are invisible.

The skill is the user's own hypothetical skill. On screen there are no agent names, no migration-product names (no Snowpark Connect, SMA, SnowConvert, CoCo or Claude Code), no API names and no vendor UI. The prompt is a generic glass pill, and 'Loaded skill:' is a plain status line with no CLI glyphs.

NULL-ordering trap (S6), verified against the Spark and Snowflake ORDER BY docs: Spark's DESC defaults to NULLS LAST, while Snowflake's DESC defaults to NULLS FIRST under the default DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING=LAST. `ORDER BY updated_at DESC NULLS LAST` is valid in both and restores Spark's result. The explicit clause stays correct even if an account changes DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING. The pill stack animates exactly this. The trap is placed in a Spark SQL (.sql) job on purpose: the Snowpark DataFrame API already emits explicit NULL ordering, so never move this beat into DataFrame code. The snippets are clause fragments, checked against the docs but not executed live.

Every count is internal to the demo and comes from one constants file: 12 jobs, 10 converted, 2 need you, 10/10 match. The 'DEMO PROJECT' chip is on screen whenever a count is visible, the check chip says 'test data', and nothing says 'guaranteed'. There are no speed, time-saved or cost figures, no clock, and no vendor benchmarks (the 5.6x/41% and 5.1x/42% figures are excluded).

The two flagged jobs (events_stream.py, churn_model.py) reflect a real limit: streaming and ML Spark code has no line-for-line equivalent on Snowflake's Spark-compatible path and needs a redesign. This is conveyed only through the filenames and 'Needs you', with no API names. The end footnote states it plainly.
'It converts. You review.' is paired with the cursor skimming every converted tile before it settles on the amber ones, so the film does not imply that the 10 converted jobs skip review.
'Same playbook', never 'same output': agents are non-deterministic, so the skill makes the steps and checks consistent, not byte-identical results.

Team shot: sharing a repo-scoped skill with teammates is accurate. Each teammate's board also lands one amber tile, so reuse does not read as guaranteed success. The skill is never shown learning or rewriting itself.

Brand safety: ember #FF7A3D and ice #38E1FF are shifted away from the Spark orange (#E25A1C) and Snowflake blue (#29B5E8). Embers are round dots and ice uses hex facets; there are no flame, star or six-arm snowflake glyphs anywhere, and no issue-tracker or agent-CLI chrome. 'Spark' and 'Snowflake' appear only as plain text.
Put a date stamp ('Sep 2026') in the video description rather than on screen, because this product area changes quickly.
openQuestions: Should S6 stay as the one code moment (the NULLS LAST trap, which pays off S1's 'missed one' and gives data engineers one concrete reason to trust the skill), or should it be cut for a code-free 32.5s version? The default is to keep it; the scene is built to be removable without retiming the others.

Voice-over or silent? The cut works fully silent, and the VO lines are written to fit at about 2 words per second. If silent, should it carry a music bed and SFX? Any audio has to be supplied as local files; no TTS is available in the container.

Should the video description (not the film) say that Snowflake ships its own built-in Spark migration skill and that the Agent Skills format works across several agents? Recommended, to head off 'is this an official tool?' comments.

Should the illustrative spark-to-snowflake/ folder (SKILL.md + references/mappings.md + scripts/check.py) be published in the code-examples repo as a companion to the video? It adds credibility, but it means writing and testing a real, working skill.
feasibilitySummary:
FEASIBILITY PROBE:
- Proven stack: Remotion 4.0.529, with every @remotion/* package pinned to the same version, React 19 and TypeScript pinned to 5.9 (npm latest is 7.x). Renders 1920×1080 at 30fps to h264.
- The probe's 150-frame test rendered in 16.8s wall clock, including about 4.6s of bundling. Simple scenes run at about 12 fps and busy scenes at about 6-7 fps on 4 CPUs.
- At those rates the 1110-frame film should render in roughly 2-5 minutes (the craft judge estimated 4-10). Run `remotion bundle` once, then render from build/.
- `remotion still` exports a 1080p PNG in about 5.5s; use it at frame 606 for the thumbnail.
- Techniques proven in the probe: spring(), evolvePath and getPointAtLength, Bézier paths with travelling objects, shiki pre-tokenised code with frame-driven typing, TransitionSeries, local audio via <Audio>, and SRT captions.
- The craft judge's micro-probe added: a 40-tile CSS-3D diagonal flip with backface-visibility renders correctly at about 6.5 fps (this is the S5 wave); a rotating textPath lens ring and interpolateColors recolours are crisp; velocity-driven SVG feGaussianBlur works as cheap motion blur.

KNOWN GOTCHAS:
1. @remotion/google-fonts FAILS here (headless Chrome rejects the proxy CA). Copy the @fontsource woff2 files into public/ and load them with @remotion/fonts loadFont(staticFile). Inter and JetBrains Mono are render-verified; Inter Tight and Instrument Serif are confirmed on npm at 5.3.0.
2. Every asset (fonts, grain PNGs, audio) must be local, because Chrome cannot fetch HTTPS at render time. Do not use --ignore-certificate-errors.
3. Set Config.setColorSpace('bt709') to get yuv420p/bt709 output; the default was yuvj420p full range.
4. --gl=angle fails. Nothing in this film needs WebGL, so keep the default GL.
5. Shader transitions cost about 2-4s per frame. None are used; the light-wipe is plain SVG/CSS.
6. From the craft probe: backdrop-filter added almost nothing visible over smooth orbs, so glass is fill + hairline + inner highlight. Dark gradients band, so the baked grain is mandatory. An absolutely positioned background painted over a static SVG, so every layer needs its own AbsoluteFill. Never put a filter on a preserve-3d ancestor.
7. There is no system ffmpeg; the compositor's bundled ffprobe works for checks when LD_LIBRARY_PATH is set.
8. The user cannot see Remotion Studio in the container, so deliver MP4 renders and PNG stills.
9. Remotion's licence is free for individuals and companies of 3 or fewer people.

BUILD PLAN: prototype the two hardest shots first, the S3 triptych hinge (about 6h) and the S5 wave with its match cut (about 4h), as stills and then as 60-frame clips. The total is roughly 26-32h, per the craft judge's estimate for this scope. The probe project is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-code-examples/2057ac15-63ed-5c0a-9a3e-3179de337167/scratchpad/remotion-probe (wave reference: out/CraftWave.mp4, out/wave_45.png).
